voices.note: the Gemara's own voice of this piska: its questions (מאי, מיבעי ליה, למה לי, אטו, ותו ליכא, מנלן), its unattributed answers and derashot on new lemmas, the narrative of 12b.7-8, 13a.22-23, 16a.4-11, 16a.14, 16a.17, its kashya/teyuvta at 14a.9 and 15a.4
R' Yehuda (bar Ilai) as cited in the baraitot of 12a.13, 13a.11, 13a.18, 14b.12, 15b.14
Mordechai, whose words the stam's narrative reports
the baraita of 14b.12: eight prophet-priests from Rachav, and R' Yehuda on Chulda
במתניתא תנא (15a.3): deeds of the fathers
מיתיבי (15a.4): the prophets of Darius's second year
תניא (15a.5): R' Yehoshua ben Korcha and the Sages on Malachi

props.gloss_en: Rav Nachman: haughtiness does not befit women; two haughty women had ugly names -- one named 'hornet' (Devorah) and one 'weasel' (Chulda)
of the hornet it is written 'she sent and called Barak' (Judg 4:6) -- she did not go to him; of the weasel 'say to the man' (2 Kgs 22:15), not 'say to the king'
Rav Nachman: Chulda was of Joshua's descendants -- here 'son of Charchas' (2 Kgs 22:14), there 'in Timnat Cheres' (Judg 2:9)
the baraita Rav Eina Saba cited: eight prophets who were priests descended from Rachav the harlot: Neriah, Baruch, Seraiah, Machseiah, Jeremiah, Chilkiah, Chanamel and Shalum
R' Yehuda: Chulda too was of Rachav's descendants -- here 'son of Tikva' (2 Kgs 22:14), there 'this cord (tikvat) of scarlet thread' (Josh 2:18)
Rav Nachman: Eina Saba (some say: black pot), from me and from you the teaching is completed: she [Rachav] converted and Joshua married her
the verse: 'Nun his son, Joshua his son' (1 Chr 7:27) -- the genealogy ends with Joshua
he had no sons; he had daughters

Ulla: wherever his name and his father's name are given in prophecy, he is known to be a prophet son of a prophet; his name and not his father's, a prophet not son of a prophet; his name and his city's, he is of that city; his name and not his city's, he is of Jerusalem

a baraita: whoever's deeds and his fathers' are obscure, and Scripture specifies one of them favourably (Zeph 1:1), he is known to be righteous son of righteous; unfavourably (Jer 41:1), wicked son of wicked
Rav Nachman: Malachi is Mordechai; why is he called Malachi? because he was second to the king (melech)
the baraita cited against him: Baruch son of Neriah, Seraiah son of Maaseiah, Daniel, Mordechai Bilshan, Chaggai, Zechariah and Malachi all prophesied in the second year of Darius
a baraita, R' Yehoshua ben Korcha: Malachi is Ezra
and the Sages say: Malachi is his name
Rav Nachman: it stands to reason as the one who says Malachi is Ezra, for in Malachi's prophecy it is written 'Judah has dealt treacherously... and married the daughter of a strange god' (Mal 2:11)
and who separated the gentile wives? Ezra, as written 'and Shechaniah son of Yechiel answered and said to Ezra: we have trespassed... and married foreign women' (Ezra 10:2)
the Rabbis taught: there were four beautiful women in the world -- Sarah, Avigail, Rachav and Esther
and according to the one who says Esther was greenish, remove Esther and insert Vashti
the Rabbis taught: Rachav aroused lust by her name, Yael by her voice, Avigail by her memory, Michal daughter of Saul by her appearance
R' Yitzchak: whoever says 'Rachav, Rachav' immediately has an emission
Rav Nachman to him: I say 'Rachav, Rachav' and it does not affect me
R' Yitzchak: when I said it, [I meant] of one who knew her and was familiar with her
